point_of_contention: Does chapter 15 fail to teach the weapon-parity lesson it asserts - i.e. is the missing-demonstration claim sound, and can a worked example repair the underlying defect in the weapon table?
ruling: The council must treat the failure-to-teach proposition as rejected: the parity lesson is to be recorded as stated and demonstrated, and a worked example must not be adopted as a remedy for any weapon-table defect. t-02 may close only on the one surviving teaching defect - the second number of the two-band range notation is never defined - while any cell-level dominance in the weapon table is carried as a separate, repricing matter to be repaired by priced cell edits alone.
reasoning: The failure claim's load-bearing premise - that only properties, range and cost vary between weapon rows - is directly contradicted by the opposing parse of the Discipline column (thirteen distinct entries across seventeen rows), which the failure side does not answer; the same side explains the absent damage column as a consequence of a locked convention barring weapons from carrying damage, so a constant damage cell is not evidence of non-teaching, and the Unarmed row printing empty cells while still resolving to floor damage is offered as that thesis in table form. The 'never demonstrated' assertion is likewise met with concrete print: two distinct improvised objects placed on one shared damage line, and three differently priced gear rows repeating that same line, matching the unarmed basic attack in the chapter that owns the cards. Independently, the refutation of the remedy is unrebutted and specific - a worked example adds no cell, so it cannot repair dominances living in the cells - and its enumeration (four strict pairs, reduced to zero by four cell edits, with a single-cell alternative shown to merely relocate a pair) is counted and unopposed; a finding that specific may not be dismissed without a counter-enumeration. Only the undefined two-band range notation is conceded as live by both the failure side and the side denying the premise.
conditions: The council must record the parity lesson as demonstrated and must not adopt a worked example as a repair for any weapon-table defect.
Closure of t-02 is limited to defining the second number of the two-band range notation, in the chapter that owns attacks or wherever the notation is home.

Any dominance finding in the weapon table is a distinct matter from teaching; if the council takes it up, it must be expressed as priced cell edits (price or range per row) rather than prose, and it may not be dismissed without a counter-enumeration.

point_of_contention: Are chapter 15's non-conforming rules defects - the vehicle-chase resolution procedure, the equipment catalog and weapon-property vocabulary absent from the lookup surfaces, the Tent's undefined exhaustion penalty, the carry-slot floor missing where players compute it, and armor slot costs that cannot be resolved?
ruling: The council must treat all of these as defects and fix them additively: rebuild the chase on the core roll, with the speed differential expressed as Boon or Bane rather than a per-side die and a numeric bonus; register the equipment catalog and the six weapon properties in the lookup surfaces; add the carry-slot floor to the character-creation derived-statistics table, leaving chapter 15 unchanged on that value; either define the exhaustion penalty or restat the Tent; and make each armor's slot cost resolvable from a lookup surface.
reasoning: The chase argument supplies the conforming counter-shape from print - the book's other race to three successes runs on the acting side's 3d6 tier result - and reports an audit finding no player-facing non-3d6 contest anywhere (the only alternate die uses being GM-facing oracle tables), which the record does not answer; a per-side single die plus a speed-scaled numeric bonus therefore stands as a second resolution procedure against a rule the owning chapter extends book-wide with no subsystem carve-out, so scoping it to vehicles does not exempt it. The remaining items are specific and checkable: sixty-nine catalogued entries and five of six property names absent from the lookup surfaces, with one property headword resolving to an unrelated ancestry trait; a Tent benefit hanging on a term that appears nowhere else in the chapter sources and has no entry in either lookup surface; a derived-statistics table printing the bare carry-slot product against a floor stated in two other chapters; and armor given a flat slot band while no armor row anywhere carries a Slots column. Every one of these is unopposed in the recorded rounds, and the one assertion of a legitimate bounded exception is rejected on the argument as presented, so on the burden of proof each stands as a defect. The single placement disagreement - where the carry-slot fix lands - resolves the same way on both sides: the character-creation table, not chapter 15.
conditions: Registration fixes must be additive to the lookup surfaces and must not alter chapter 15's existing rules.
The carry-slot correction lands in the character-creation derived-statistics table; chapter 15 requires no change on that value.
The Tent must be either given a defined exhaustion penalty or restated so its stated benefit is resolvable from the book.

Any chase rebuild must conform to the core resolution (3d6, acting side rolls, the opponent's ability as Challenge), with the speed differential expressed as Boon or Bane rather than a numeric bonus or a separate die.
